texts.facts: In the present case, Detailed Accident Report (DAR) was filed on 09.09.2015 regarding a Road Traffic Accident, which took place on 10.07.2015 at 12.30 PM at Wazirabad Road, Surghat Bus Stand, Wazirabad, Delhi. In this accident, the petitioner Rajan @ Raju sustained grievous injuries and the accident took place with a vehicle i.e. TSR bearing registration No. DL-1NCR-1728 driven and owned by respondent no. 1 Vishnu and insured with respondent no. 2 Bharti Axa General Insurance Company Ltd. (which was merged with ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd. vide order dated 03.05.2023). 2. It emerged from the DAR that on 10.07.2015, Sh. Rajan @ Raju who used to supply homemade food tiffin was going by foot from his home to his sister's home. He was standing at Wazirabad Surghat Bus Stand, Delhi when suddenly a driver of TSR bearing No. DL- 1NCR-1728 namely Vishnu came at a very high speed and hit the petitioner. Due to the said accident, the petitioner fell on the road and sustained injury on his left side back. Thereafter, respondent no. 1 took him to the Trauma Centre Hospital in his TSR. From there, the doctors referred him to the LNJP Hospital and he called his wife Sonu Anand. It is the case of the petitioner that respondent no. 1was driving his TSR rashly and negligently and due to his negligence, the accident took place. The IO recorded the statement of the petitioner and prepared the site plan at the instance of Sh. Vijay Kumar, brother-in-law of the MACT No. 57749/16 Rajan @ Raju Vs. Vishnu Tarun and another page 2 of 39 injured Rajan @ Raju. TSR bearing no. DL-1NCR-1728 was seized and deposited in the Malkhana. During investigation, driver of the offending vehicle i.e. TSR got arrested and his statement was recorded and later on, he was released on bail. The documents pertaining to the vehicle were verified. Mechanical inspection of TSR was got done by ASI. Later, the TSR was released on superdari. The result of MLC was obtained as 'grievous' and section 338 IPC was added. Charge- sheet/challan was filed before the concerned court of Ld. MM and DAR was filed before this Tribunal on 09.09.2015. 3. No written statement/reply to the DAR was filed on behalf of the respondent no.1 (driver-cum-owner) despite various opportunities and therefore, the opportunity to file the same was closed. However, respondent no. 2/ insurance company had filed its reply wherein it was stated that they were not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner as the petitioner did not have a valid and effective permit in respect of the vehicle as on the date of accident. ISSUES FRAMED 4. On 03.05.2023, an application under section 151 CPC was moved on behalf of respondent no. 2/ insurance company for impleadment/ substitution of ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd. in place of Bharti Axa General Insurance Co. Ltd. which was duly allowed. Evidence: 6. Ld. Local Commissioner was appointed for recording of evidence of the parties who filed the report on 10.10.2023. The petitioner Sh. Rajan Anand @ Raju was examined as PW-1 and Dr. Anil Ranjan, CMO, Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, Pitampura, Delhi was examined as PW-2. PE was closed. Despite opportunities, respondent no.2/ the insurance company did not lead RE. 7. The petitioner filed the Form XIV. Financial statement of the petitioner was recorded. Final arguments were heard on behalf of all the parties on 23.01.2024. The factum of accident: 11. In this matter to prove the occurrence of the accident as well as the rashness and negligence on the part of the driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1, the petitioner (PW-1) in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A, had deposed as under:- "2. The aforesaid accident was occurred on the fault of driver of the offending vehicle who did not blow any horn and did not pay attention towards going pedstrains on the road, who had driven the vehicle very rash and negligently and in contravention of traffic rules and regulations without caring safety of others of road users came from main road. 3. The police seized the offending TSR driver was arrested, an FIR No. 483/15 dated 10.07.2015, u/s. 279/337 IPC was registered under PS Timarpur, A MLC No. 6142/15 was conducted by the Doctor of Trauma Centre (LNJP) Hospital. 4. The accident has been absolutely caused due to the MACT No. 57749/16 Rajan @ Raju Vs. Vishnu Tarun and another page 6 of 39 negligence on the part of respondent no. 1/driver cum owner who is liable to pay the compensation, the offending vehicle was driven rashly and negligently, the driver is also owner of the offending vehicle whose vehicle was insured with the insurance company i.e. respondent no. 2. All the respondents are liable jointly and severally to pay compensation to the petitioner under the law of Torts, MV Act and other provisions of law. 5. The injured is a self employed and used to supply Tiffin Box, The injured was earning Rs. 20,000/- per month. Since, the accident was occurred the injured is on the bed getting treatment. The injured got treatment from the Hospital and Private Clinic. The injured was admitted on 10.07.2015 and discharged on 15.07.2015 is sustained Palvis Fracture (Fracture of Neck of humer (L). More than Rs. 25,000/- spent upon his treatment. The injured was operated, a Rod was inserted. More expenses will likely to become in future and a disablement may come. The injured is on bed and is not in position to do work of his occupation. He is totally unfit for doing his routine work of nature also. He has difficulty in walking, climbing, riding the cycle or setting properly. The injured is compelled to keep a servant to look after the injured. The injured is payment Rs. 6000/- per month. The injured has a very difficulty to collect the daily meal as his occupation is already stopped he become job less, many liabilities are upon the injured his children are in half way of study as they are facing also shortage of money. His wife is also compelled to work elsewhere due to unavoidable accident this accident has ruined the life of the Rajan@Raju (I)(Fir48315Timarpur) vs Vishnu (Bharti Axa Gen. Ins.) on 26 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60664563/ 4 petitioner. The aforesaid accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by respondent no. 1. All the respondents are liable to pay compensation jointly and severally. 6. The petitioner/deponent is filing some relevant documents which are as under : PW-1 Medical Record & Discharge Summary colly page. PW-1/2 Medical Bill colly page MACT No. 57749/16 Rajan @ Raju Vs. Vishnu Tarun and another page 7 of 39 PW-1/3 Voter ID Card PW-1/4 Disability certificate PW-1/5 DAR Report . " 12. PW-1, Rajan @ Raju, has proved the factum of the accident and the identity of the respondent no. 1. He has unequivocally testified that respondent no. 1 was riding the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL-1NCR-1728 at a very high speed, leading to the accident due to his rash and negligent driving. His medical condition has been noted as: "Inability to bear weight on affected limb (L)" and also "(L) lower limb in ext relation. Tenderness + near greater trochanter, Ab (n) mobility + hip joint tenderness + active SLR (-). no metor sensory deficit. Distal pulses well palpable." 18. Further, an application seeking direction to the Medical Superintendent, Aruna Asaf Ali Hospital, Delhi, to examine the petitioner and issue permanent disability certificate, was moved on MACT No. 57749/16 Rajan @ Raju Vs. Vishnu Tarun and another page 10 of 39 behalf of the petitioner, which was allowed and the concerned Medical Superintendent of Aruna Asaf Ali Hospital, Delhi, was directed to examine the petitioner to assess his disability and to file his disability certificate. Pursuant to such order, the disability certificate bearing no. 222 dated 02.11.2016 was received from the Office of Medical Superintendent, Aruna Asaf Ali Govt. Hospital, 5 Rajpur Road, Delhi- 110054. The petitioner/ injured has claimed Rs. 6,000/- per month for 7 months under this head, however, there is no cogent evidence on record for the money spent by the petitioner upon an attendant. Perusal of record reveals that PE was concluded on 08.08.2023. Thus, the petitioner will be Rajan@Raju (I)(Fir48315Timarpur) vs Vishnu (Bharti Axa Gen. Ins.) on 26 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60664563/ 16 entitled to interest w.e.f. 09.09.2013 to 01.02.2019 and again from 08.08.2023 till realization. Hence, till the date of award, the total period for which the petitioner is entitled to interest is 5 years 11 months and 11 days. The Financial Statement of petitioner/injured was recorded by this Court/Tribunal.

Total permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform any avocation or employment related activities as a result of the accident.

But if any of the disabilities enumerated in section 2(i) of the Disabilities Act are the result of injuries sustained in a motor accident, they can be permanent disabilities for the purpose of claiming compensation.
7.
The percentage of permanent disability is expressed by the Doctors with reference to the whole body, or more often than not, with reference to a particular limb.

When a disability certificate states MACT No. 57749/16 Rajan @ Raju Vs. Vishnu Tarun and another page 14 of 39 that the injured has suffered permanent disability to an extent of 45% of the left lower limb, it is not the same as 45%
permanen

The extent of disability of a limb (or part of the body) expressed in terms of a percentage of the total functions of that limb, obviously cannot be assumed to be the extent of disability of the whole body.

If there is 60% permanent disability of the right hand and 80% permanent disability of left leg, it does not mean that the extent of permanent disability with reference to the whole body is 140% (that is 80% plus 60%).

If different parts of the body have suffered different percentages of disabilities, the sum total thereof expressed in terms of the permanent disability with reference to the whole body, cannot obviously exceed 100%.
8.

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacit
The Tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

In most of the cases, the percentage of economic loss, that is, percentage of loss of earning capacity,
arising from a permanent disability will be different from the percentage of permanent disability.

Some Tribunals wrongly assume that in all cases, a particular extent (percentage) of permanent disability would result in a corresponding loss of earning capacity, and consequently, if the evidence produced show 45% as the permanent disabil

In most of the cases, equating the extent (percentage) of loss of earning capacity to the extent (percentage) of permanent disability will result in award of either too low or too high a compensation.

What requires to be assessed by the Tribunal is the effect of the permanently disability on the earning capacity of the injured; and after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of a percentage of the income, it has to be quantifie

Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so the extent of such permanent disability.

This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence: (i) whether the disablement is permanent or temporary; (ii) if the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent part
If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.
But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will proceed to ascertain its extent.

After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.

Be that as it may."

The assessment of future medical expenses would depend upon specific medical evidence/advise for further treatment and costs thereof.

The process would involve determination/assessment of lump-sum amounts under those heads.

In the case of assessment of loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability,
this Tribunal needs to first ascertain whether the disability noted/assessed by the medical board is temporary or permanent in nature.
If the disability is permanent in nature, then whether it is a total permanent disability or partial permanent disability.

If the disability has been referred/expressed in percentage terms, in reference to any specific limb then the effect of such disability of the limb on the function of entire body has to be ascertained.

The Tribunal then also needs to ascertain whether the claimant is totality disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on activities and functions
After ascertaining the functional disability through the above process, the Tribunal needs to workout the loss of earning capacity per month.
